newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says he committed to free trade with Chile.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says he committed to free trade with Chile.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday he was committed to completing a free trade agreement with Chile and Congress needed to pass legislation that would speed up that process.
"Our administration remains committed to concluding a comprehensive free trade agreement with Chile," Clinton said at a joint news conference with Chilean President Eduardo Frei.

Clinton said he told Frei during their meeting that he wants to get so-called "fast track" trade negotiation authority from Congress. That would allow U.S. trade officials to negotiate an agreement with Chile without fear it will later be changed by Congress.
"I believe we must have fast track authority to conclude new trade agreements that open markets to America's products and that advance our values," Clinton said.

Chile was invited to join the North American Free Trade Agreement, which links the United States, Canada and Mexico, at the first Summit of the Americas in Miami in December 1994. Chile has concluded agreements with Canada, Mexico and other Latin American countries and is negotiating a deal with the European Union. But the lack of fast track authority has delayed negotiations with the United States.
"The United States simply cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while others share in the fruits of Latin America's remarkable growth," Clinton said.
